note: Signals are evidence to weigh, not a formula and not proof. Crowd prices are a benchmark, never an input.

signals.name: CISA KEV additions
signals.method: blocks = sums of non-overlapping 7-day windows counted back from the last complete UTC day (daily series; null days drop the block) or the weekly values (weekly series); latest = the newest block, fit = the previous up to 12 blocks. TREND: Theil-Sen slope of log(count+1) over the fit blocks, reported as %/week when Kendall tau p < 0.05 and |slope| >= 5%/week; a trend is never an anomaly. ANOMALY (spike or drop): latest against the trend extrapolated one block ahead, r = log(latest+1) - log(expected+1); flagged when |r| >= log(1.8), |r| >= 3 x the median absolute deviation of the fit residuals, the larger of latest and expected is >= 5, and there are at least 4 fit blocks. baseline = median of the fit blocks (shown for scale only). Known gaps: blocks are not calendar-aligned, GitHub counts of the newest days can still be backfilled, holidays are not tagged (method reviewed by a second model, 2026-10-21).
signals.means: More vulnerabilities confirmed as exploited in the wild: a wider attack surface that an autonomous or AI-assisted attacker could use.
signals.not_proof: KEV is about all software, not AI; additions follow CISA's review rhythm and say nothing about who exploited what.

Every month by incident date is open (later posts can still fill it).
